                                      PUC DOCKET NO. 59475

APPLICATION OF ONCOR ELECTRIC                                   §
DELIVERY COMPANY LLC AND LCRA                                   §            BEFORE THE
TRANSMISSION SERVICES CORPORATION                               §
TO AMEND THEIR CERTIFICATES OF                                  §         THE STATE OFFICE
CONVENIENCE AND NECESSITY FOR THE                               §
BELL COUNTY EAST SWITCH TO BIG HILL                             §                  OF
SUBSTATION 765-KV TRANSMISSION LINE                             §
PROJECT IN BELL, BURNET, CONCHO,                                §         ADMINISTRATIVE
CORYELL, LAMPASAS, LLANO, MASON,                                §
MCCULLOCH, MENARD, MILAM, MILLS,                                §             HEARINGS
SAN SABA, SCHLEICHER, TOM GREEN,                                §
AND WILLIAMSON COUNTIES                                         §




                                         KEVIN KENNEDY’S

       MOTION TO REJECT APPLICANTS’ MOTION TO STRIKE TESTIMONY

               TO THE STATE OFFICE OF ADMINISTRATIVE HEARINGS



        Kevin Kennedy ("Mr. Kennedy, I, me, etc.”) respectfully and timely files this request that

the State Office of Administrative Hearings ("SOAH") Administrative Law Judges ("ALJs")

reject Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC’s (“Oncor’s”) and LCRA Transmission Services

Corporation’s (“LCRA’s”)(collectively, “Applicants’”) motion to strike Mr. Kennedy’s

testimony, which was based on their incorrect presumption that he is not an expert.




KENNEDY 59475 – Motion to reject Applicants’ motion to strike testimony                 Page 1 of 6
                                            I.   BACKGROUND

Applicants’ motion to strike Mr. Kennedy’s testimony

        On May 18, 2026, the Applicants filed a motion to strike intervenor testimony (59475-

4726), which included a request to strike a portion of Mr. Kennedy’s direct testimony (59475-

4103). The Applicants did not number the pages in their motion, but the relevant text is in

Attachment A of their motion on pages 22 and 23 of their posted .PDF.

        The Applicants requested to strike the following testimony, based on Mr. Kennedy not

being an expert:

        "The North American Electric Reliability Corporation (NERC), is a not-for-Direct profit,

international regulatory authority dedicated to effectively and efficiently Testimony reducing

risks to the reliability and security of the bulk power system. NERC provides guidance to

Applicants in FAC-003-5 Transmission Vegetation Interchange Management. The table on the

following page, indicating minimum vegetative Item No. clearance requirements for high voltage

transmission lines, is taken from that 4103 document.

        The minimum vegetation clearance distance from a 765-kV conductor is 11.9 feet for

elevations between 1,000 and 2,000 feet above sea level. This standard should have been used,

with some reasonable allowance for growth, striking balance with maintenance, the Applicants'

duty to protect the environment, and the landowner's right to be protected from adverse harm.

The Applicants should have also considered the different plant species and their individual

growth potentials. The Applicants should have provided an in-depth, detailed vegetation

preservation and management plan rather than a scorched earth, we need to take everything to

bare ground approach. They appear to be wholly lacking the integrity needed to be bestowed

responsibility of the preservation and protection of 10,000 acres of land, which they do not own.



KENNEDY 59475 – Motion to reject Applicants’ motion to strike testimony                  Page 2 of 6
         This disregard for environmental stewardship, and the total lack of common decency and

respect of property rights owed to the landowners, foreshadows how the Applicants will likely

conduct their implementation, construction and maintenance of Import Path 2." P. 5-6.


Mr. Kennedy’s qualifications as an expert, relevant to his testimony
        Mr. Kennedy is a licensed professional engineer in the State of Texas (TX PE 72984),

with over 35 years of voluminous engineering experience and extensive expertise relevant to

these proceedings and his testimony.

        He grew up farming and ranching on his family’s cow / calf operation, being trained and

guided by his parents to care for the land, the environment, and all the flora and fauna.

        Mr. Kennedy attended Texas A&M University and graduated in 1986 with a Bachelor of

Science degree in Civil Engineering. His professional engineering career was almost exclusively

in the field of planning and design of large highway projects across Texas. As a consulting

engineer, he served as a Project Manager on significant projects statewide for the Texas

Department of Transportation (“TxDOT”), the North Texas Tollway Authority, and the Central

Texas Regional Mobility, in addition to numerous Counties and municipalities.

         In 1998, Mr. Kennedy founded Kennedy Consulting, Inc. (“KCI”) and served as its

President and sole shareholder. KCI was acquired by Johnson, Mirmiran & Thompson, Inc.

(“JMT”), (ranked #45 nationally in ENR’s 2026 Top 500 Design Firms) in 2016, though Mr.

Kennedy continued to serve as President of KCI until 2018. Prior to starting KCI, he was a Vice

President with Kimley-Horn & Associates, Inc. (“KHA”), (ranked #8 nationally in ENR’s 2026

Top 500 Design Firms), where he served as Division Leader of KHA’s Central Region Design

Division.

        Throughout Mr. Kennedy’s career, he used his expertise to lead the development of

major highway planning and design projects, including numerous new-location or green-field


KENNEDY 59475 – Motion to reject Applicants’ motion to strike testimony                     Page 3 of 6
 projects for TxDOT that were required to follow State and Federal regulations, including

development of Environmental Assessments in compliance with the National Environmental

Policy Act (“NEPA”). The processes and requirements of these linear, new-location routing

studies and environmental assessments are very similar in nature to those of this linear, new-

location transmission line routing study and environmental assessment.

        Mr. Kennedy was the highly qualified engineer in responsible charge to collected

environmental constraint data, identified potential route options, coordinated with the public,

analyze and refine route alternatives, and eventually provide a signed and sealed engineered

schematic design of the proposed facility and a NEPA compliant Environmental Assessment that

would be reviewed and approved by appropriate State and Federal resources agencies, including

Clean Water Act - Section 404 permitting through the US Army Corps of Engineers, and

eventually approved by the Federal Highway Administration. Mr. Kennedy was a recognized

expert in these areas and TxDOT sought his expertise on many, many projects. Mr. Kennedy and

KCI served as the prime engineering consultant on major projects in twenty-two TxDOT

Districts, a service area that covered almost the entire State.

        Mr. Kennedy also was the engineer in responsible charge of many final design highway

projects that provided all construction documents including plans, specifications and estimates

(“PS&E”) for the construction of major highway projects. A key component of these PS&E

projects was compliance with State and Federal regulations concerning stormwater pollution

prevention plans, requiring approval from the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality

(“TCEQ”). The designs, plans and permitting documents prepared by Mr. Kennedy included the

plans and specifications for the removal of existing vegetation as necessary for construction of

the facility, temporary grading and seeding, temporary erosion control devices and other best

management practices (“BMPs”) to control sediment, maintenance requirements for BMPS, and


KENNEDY 59475 – Motion to reject Applicants’ motion to strike testimony                  Page 4 of 6
 permanent seeding with native grasses including watering requirements to establish sufficient

ground cover.

        A key component of Mr. Kennedy’s construction documents was preservation of

sensitive natural features. His team of environmental specialists would conduct field

reconnaissance to identify and delineate the boundaries of sensitive locations. Mr. Kennedy

would note these areas in the plans and provide specifications to direct the Contractor on how

these areas were to be protected. This might include fencing off areas to prohibit access,

protection of potential threatened or endangered species habitat, protections for nesting birds and

bat colonies, no-mow areas, etc.

        Mr. Kennedy also had multiple projects in the Edwards Aquifer recharge zone,

contributing zone and transition zone, which require TCEQ permitting for Water Pollution

Abatement Plans or Contributing Zone Plans. These projects required Mr. Kennedy to produce

plans and specifications to direct the Contractor to protect existing groundcover, control

discharge of sedimentation, protect and avoid known recharge features, as well as to identify and

protect any unknown recharge features, if encountered, and to compete all TCEQ required

inspection and reporting requirements.

        In addition to Mr. Kennedy’s extensive expertise as a professional engineer and project

manager, he has been a steward of the land all his life. He has worked tirelessly to restore his

family ranch in Burnet County to its historic native state. He has carefully and systematically

controlled brush, preserved and trimmed existing native hardwood trees, taken extensive

measures to control the spread of oak wilt, planted native trees, combatted invasive and

undesirable plants, planted hundreds of acres of native grasses, controlled erosion, etc., etc. In

recognition of these efforts, several years ago the Texas Forest Service named Mr. Kennedy

conservationist of the year for Burnet County.


KENNEDY 59475 – Motion to reject Applicants’ motion to strike testimony                      Page 5 of 6
                                                II. PRAYER

        Mr. Kennedy is a highly qualified and knowledgeable licensed professional engineer and

expert on matters associated with the protection and management of the natural environment as it

relates to the construction and long-term maintenance of linear infrastructure projects. He is

confident his expertise and knowledge compare favorably to that of the Applicants’ experts Ms.

Casey Petty and Mr. Russell Marusak.

        Mr. Kennedy respectfully requests the SOAH ALJs recognize Mr. Kennedy’s

qualifications as an expert in the matters of preservation and protection of natural features, reject

the Applicants’ motion to strike Mr. Kennedy’s testimony, and allow his testimony to stand.




Date Signed: May 19, 2026



Respectfully submitted,

Kevin Kennedy




By:     /s/ J .   Kevin Kennedy

630 County Road 282

Bertram, Texas 78605

Telephone: (512) 639-1720

Email: jkkennedy.tx@gmail.com
